### The “Best” Sushi Restaurants in Los Angeles (as of 2026)

> **Note:** “Best” is a mix of Michelin‑star recognition, critical acclaim, local buzz, and overall dining experience. Prices vary from casual to high‑end, so pick the one that fits your vibe and budget.

| Rank | Restaurant | Michelin Status | Price Range | Highlights | Address |
|------|------------|-----------------|-------------|------------|---------|
| 1 | **Sushi Gen** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $70–$120 per person | Classic Edomae style, fresh toro, impeccable service. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
| 2 | **Sushi Park** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $80–$140 per person | Innovative omakase, seasonal ingredients, intimate setting. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
| 3 | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $90–$150 per person | Chef‑driven, minimalist décor, focus on quality over quantity. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
| 4 | **Sushi Kappo** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $80–$130 per person | Traditional kaiseki, meticulous plating, serene atmosphere. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
| 5 | **Sushi O** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $70–$120 per person | Contemporary twist on classics, vibrant interior, great for groups. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
| 6 | **Sushi Nori** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $60–$110 per person | Fresh fish, creative rolls, friendly staff. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
| 7 | **Sushi Tatsu** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $70–$120 per person | Authentic Edomae, chef’s choice menu, cozy setting. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |

| 9 | **Sushi Kappo** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $80–$130 per person | Traditional kaiseki, meticulous plating, serene atmosphere. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |
|10 | **Sushi O** | 1 Michelin Star (2024) | $70–$120 per person | Contemporary twist on classics, vibrant interior, great for groups. | 1120 S. La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028 |

> **Why the cluster?**  
> The Michelin‑starred sushi scene in LA is concentrated around the **Sushi Gen** complex on La Brea (the “Sushi Gen” block). These restaurants share a common kitchen but offer distinct menus and atmospheres. If you’re looking for a Michelin‑starred experience, any of them will satisfy.

---

## Quick Picks by Category

| Category | Recommendation | Why It Stands Out |
|----------|----------------|-------------------|
| **All‑round Michelin‑starred** | **Sushi Gen** | Classic Edomae, legendary toro, impeccable service. |
| **Omakase lovers** | **Sushi Park** | Chef‑curated tasting menu, seasonal focus. |
| **Budget‑friendly yet high quality** | **Sushi Nori** | Great value, fresh fish, friendly vibe. |
| **Family‑friendly** | **Sushi O** | Spacious, great for groups, modern décor. |
| **Hidden gem** | **Sushi Tetsu** | Intimate, chef‑driven, minimalist décor. |

---

## Practical Tips

1. **Reservations** – All Michelin‑starred spots book up fast. Reserve 2–3 months in advance if possible.
2. **Dress Code** – Smart casual is fine; some places have a more formal vibe.
3. **Tip** – 15–20 % is standard for sushi in LA. If you’re paying a flat‑rate omakase, the tip is usually included.
4. **Dietary Needs** – Most places can accommodate allergies or dietary restrictions; just let the host know at the time of booking.

---
